text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Kuwait welcomes United Nations warning to former occupier Iraq. The Security Council unanimously warned Iraq it faced further sanctions if it did not allow U.N. arms inspectors to search sensitive sites.

- Kuwait's Defence Minister Sheikh Salem Sabah al-Salem al-Sabah says Kuwait strongly supports international efforts to ban anti-personnel mines. Since the 1991 Gulf War Kuwait has cleared more than one million mines and officials say millions more were planted by Iraq in the tiny Gulf Arab state.
- British Foreign Office Minister Derek Fatchett to arrive in Kuwait on Monday to discuss pending arms deals and stress London's support to the security of Gulf Arab states.
- Kuwait City Municipality asks government to impose harsher penalties on traders who sell expired food.
- Kuwait to host next March the first international meeting on the role of the family and religion towards drug abuse.
